answer.rationale: Memory c2 supplies precedent that switching primary supply to a low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and clean invoicing, which directly serves the mandated 18% spend cut now that the incumbent has refused to move on price. However, c1 shows renewals with the incumbent stayed stable, and c3 shows adding a second source removed a single point of failure during a shortage, while c6 shows multi-year commitments with an incumbent unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope. Given the contract expires in 14 days, the line runs at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, and I have only one decision this cycle, switching primary carries too much delivery risk at this stage; a small, guarded test of an alternate vendor plus a one-cycle renewal with the incumbent to cover the immediate window offers the strongest path to lowering TCO without raising delivery risk. I will limit verification to memory c2 to confirm the low-cost vendor migration cost and timeline were stable, and I will defer a full primary switch until next cycle once the alternate vendor's quality and delivery performance are proven against incumbent benchmarks drawn from c1, c4, and c6.
